issues.legal_issue: Dismissal for non-prosecution of an application to fix standard rent does not itself fix the rent or establish a genuine dispute about the amount payable.
material_facts: The agreed monthly rent was ₹30, and both sides accepted that no standard rent had been finally fixed under the statutory procedure.
The tenant's application to fix standard rent was dismissed for non-prosecution.
issues.conclusion: The dismissal did not amount to a fixation of standard rent. In the absence of a genuine dispute, the agreed rent remained the standard rent for the purposes of the case.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 5(10) and 11 of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, standard rent is fixed through the procedure specified by the Act. Dismissal of an application for non-prosecution is not such a fixation; where the tenant has not pursued the application, the court may infer that it was not a bona fide application and that no genuine dispute about standard rent or permitted increases existed.

predicates.nonpayment_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking possession on the ground that the tenant had not paid rent.
predicates.agreed_rent_identified: The parties agreed on the rent payable for the premises.
predicates.standard_rent_application_dismissed_for_: The tenant's application to fix standard rent was dismissed because the tenant did not prosecute it.

issues.definition: When a nonpayment eviction proceeding involves an identified agreed rent and the tenant's standard-rent application was dismissed for non-prosecution, the agreed rent remains the applicable standard rent.

issues.legal_issue: Where rent is payable monthly, the amount payable is not genuinely disputed, and the tenant neglects to pay arrears of at least six months after the required demand notice, the court must grant eviction under the statutory arrears provision.
material_facts: The rent was payable monthly, and the agreed monthly rent was ₹30.
The tenant's application to fix standard rent was dismissed for non-prosecution, and the court found no real dispute about standard rent or permitted increases.
Rent had remained unpaid for more than six months, and the landlord served a notice demanding payment before bringing the eviction suit.
issues.conclusion: The case fell within section 12(3)(a); because its requirements were not met by the tenant, the court was bound to pass an eviction decree.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(3)(a) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, applies where rent is payable monthly, there is no dispute about standard rent or permitted increases, arrears have continued for six months or more, and the tenant neglects to pay within one month after the demand notice under section 12(2). Under Vora Abbasbhai Alimahomed v. Haji Gulamnabi Haji Safibhai, [1964] 5 S.C.R. 157, the court is bound to decree eviction when the statutory requirements apply and are not complied with.

rule.if: nonpayment_eviction_proceeding and monthly_rent and no_genuine_rent_dispute and arrears_for_at_least_six_months and demand_notice_served and tenant_neglected_payment_after_notice

predicates.nonpayment_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking possession because the tenant had not paid rent.
predicates.no_genuine_rent_dispute: The tenant did not establish a genuine dispute about the rent or permitted increases payable.
predicates.arrears_for_at_least_six_months: The rent or permitted increases remained unpaid for six months or longer.
predicates.demand_notice_served: The landlord served the tenant with a written demand for the rent or permitted increases due.
predicates.tenant_neglected_payment_after_notice: The tenant did not pay the amount due within the required period after receiving the demand notice.

issues.definition: In a nonpayment eviction proceeding, if monthly rent is undisputed, at least six months of arrears exist, and the tenant neglects payment after notice, an eviction decree is required.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant seeking the protection available under the statutory payment procedure must make the required payments or tenders on time and continue making them regularly; failure to do so removes the case from that protection.
material_facts: The court fixed interim rent at ₹25 per month and directed the tenant to deposit both arrears and future rent at that rate.
The tenant did not comply with the deposit directions, and the application in which interim rent had been fixed was later dismissed for non-prosecution.
The tenant admitted that rent had not been paid regularly as contemplated by the court's order.
issues.conclusion: The tenant did not satisfy the payment requirements for protection under section 12(3)(b), and the defaults deprived him of the Act's protection against eviction.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(3)(b) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, bars eviction only where the tenant pays or tenders the rent and permitted increases due by the first hearing or another date fixed by the court, continues to pay or tender them regularly until final decision, and pays costs as directed. Shah Dhansukhlal Chaganlal v. Dalichand Virchand Shroff, [1968] 3 S.C.R. 346, holds that failure to deposit rent regularly as required takes the case outside that protection. The explanation to section 12 provides a rule of evidence concerning readiness and willingness; it does not excuse non-compliance with the payment requirements.

rule.if: nonpayment_eviction_proceeding and tenant_seeks_payment_based_protection and court_fixed_payment_requirements and tenant_failed_to_pay_or_tender_as_required

predicates.nonpayment_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking possession because the tenant had not paid rent.
predicates.tenant_seeks_payment_based_protection: The tenant relied on statutory protection that depends on paying or tendering rent during the proceeding.
predicates.court_fixed_payment_requirements: The court specified amounts or timing for payment or deposit of rent during the proceeding.
predicates.tenant_failed_to_pay_or_tender_as_requir: The tenant failed to make the payments or tenders required by the court or to continue them regularly.

issues.definition: A tenant in a nonpayment eviction proceeding who seeks payment-based protection loses that protection by failing to meet the court's payment requirements.

issues.legal_issue: Inability to pay rent because of a lack of means does not by itself establish readiness and willingness to pay, and the court cannot excuse non-compliance with statutory payment conditions on compassionate grounds.
material_facts: The tenant said he was poor and unable to pay the total amount due at once, and later relied on difficulty finding money to pay rent.
The appellate court had found defaults in payment, and the High Court did not set those factual findings aside.
The tenant had not complied with the payment requirements governing statutory protection.
issues.conclusion: The tenant could not be treated as ready and willing to pay, and his financial hardship did not entitle him to statutory protection from eviction. The Court restored the eviction decree, while allowing a limited, conditional delay before it could be executed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 12(1) of the Bombay Rents, Hotel and Lodging House Rates Control Act, 1947, protects a tenant who pays, or is ready and willing to pay, standard rent and permitted increases and performs the other consistent conditions of the tenancy, subject to the limitations in sections 12(2) and 12(3). Readiness and willingness must be assessed by compliance with the Act; inability to pay for want of means is not enough. The Act gives courts no power to condone statutory violations on compassionate grounds. Shah Dhansukhlal Chaganlal v. Dalichand Virchand Shroff, [1968] 3 S.C.R. 346, was applied.

predicates.nonpayment_eviction_proceeding: A landlord brought a proceeding seeking possession because the tenant had not paid rent.
predicates.tenant_unable_to_pay_for_lack_of_means: The tenant's inability to pay rent resulted from a lack of financial means.
predicates.tenant_failed_to_comply_with_statutory_p: The tenant did not meet the payment or tender conditions required for statutory protection.

issues.definition: In a nonpayment eviction proceeding, a tenant's lack of means combined with failure to meet statutory payment conditions does not establish readiness to pay or preserve protection from eviction.
